payload.rationale: No forecast or observational evidence was supplied, so this estimate rests on climatology for Miami International Airport in mid-September. The normal daily high around Sep 19 is roughly 88-89°F, making the 88-89° bin the modal two-degree bucket. Historical mid-September highs at MIA cluster tightly: most days fall between 86 and 91°F, with rainy or cloudy days (common in the late wet season, especially with tropical moisture) pulling highs down to 83-86°F, and drier, sunnier days pushing to 90-92°F. A two-degree bin at the center of that distribution typically captures roughly one-third of outcomes. Too high: if a tropical disturbance, front, or widespread convection affects South Florida that day, highs could easily be held in the low-to-mid 80s; alternatively a hot, dry pattern makes 90-92° quite common in September, and 90° alone is often the single most frequent value, which would put the outcome just above the bin. Too low: 88-89° is arguably the most likely two-degree window climatologically, and if the synoptic pattern near the cutoff was typical (seabreeze-driven afternoon storms after a warm morning), 88-89° highs are very common; also Weather Company rounding could nudge borderline 87.5 or 89.5 readings into the bin. Without any current forecast or observed conditions, I stay near the climatological base rate rather than shading in either direction.
limitations: No current forecast, model guidance, or observed conditions were supplied for Sep 19, 2026.
Estimate relies entirely on climatological memory of mid-September Miami high temperatures, which may be imprecise.
Weather Company reported value may differ from NWS/ASOS observations due to rounding or data source differences.
